Action Plan:
1. Prescribe an antibiotic course for presumed lower urinary tract infection (options discussed: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim) — one tablet twice daily for 3 days as discussed; patient to start medication today. (Specific agent selection and tablet strength not documented.)
2. Advise increased oral fluids and symptomatic measures; cranberry juice suggested as an adjunct.
3. Advise avoidance of sexual activity while symptomatic; continue barrier contraception (condoms) and avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve.
4. Advise patient to contact clinic or return if symptoms have not improved by the end of the week or sooner if she develops fever, back/flank pain, or worsened systemic illness (concern for possible ascending infection/pyelonephritis).
5. Recommend pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy if patient is concerned or if symptoms do not improve.
6. Documented allergy: clindamycin — causes swelling; avoid prescribing clindamycin.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

- Medications: None regular; recently tried over-the-counter bicarbonate a couple of days ago (ineffective).
- Allergies: Clindamycin — swelling reaction.
- Social history: Student (biology), lives in flat with friends, non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially on weekends.
